trigger: replica system clock skewed against the database by hours, then a fleet usage read
classification_rationale: the fresh/stale split compared a replica-clock instant with usage_state.last_seen authored by the database clock; reporting_devices, stale_devices and the fresh flags were wrong with no signal to the caller
summary: Freshness mixed two clocks. Fixed (adapted by the Architect: carry the width, not an instant): DexUsageQuery::fresh_since_epoch is now fresh_secs and the one statement compares us.last_seen >= now() - $10::bigint * interval '1 second' on the database clock; the observation window stays on the request instant. Pinned by a [pg] owner case at DB now()-47h, -50h and a device with no usage_state row under skews of 0, +-36 h and +-49 h, and a seam assert that a skewed injected instant leaves the width unchanged.

Fixed (adapted): the route now refuses it before the audit and the read with the shared mgmt_group_id_ok predicate (1..256 bytes, no C0 control or NUL or DEL, valid UTF-8), which already covers what app_perf_param_valid plus is_valid_utf8 would and is already included in the route file, so no third copy and no new include. A 400, no audit row, no read.

adjudicated_by: Kimi K2.8, external adversarial reviewer (second adversarial pass, finding K2), not the author of this change; independence is asserted, the field is free text
adjudication_rationale: The investigation resolved the speculative claim: agent-stamped observed_at is cut at the request instant (exclusive upper bound) exactly as every other DEX read cuts its window, documented in dex_usage_model.hpp and dex_api.cpp; a skewed replica or agent clock moves only the event tail of the window, the coverage counts no longer move, and the caller sees as_of. Reclassified from I3 to I8 (a small, bounded shift of the exposure-rate numerator on a documented convention), so the derived band is LOW. A design change (cut events against the database clock with a receipt column) is not a fix-round item.
summary: Resolved: observation-window clock asymmetry is a documented standing DEX convention (Kimi K2). No change in this change.
